title: FastFlip: Compositional SDC Resiliency Analysis
problem: Error injection analyses for Silent Data Corruption (SDC) resiliency are prohibitively expensive and must rerun from scratch after code changes, making them impractical for iterative development workflows such as regression testing.
motivation: High recurring cost of full re-analysis after each code modification prevents adoption of software-directed resiliency analysis in standard software engineering practices.
method: FastFlip combines empirical error injection with symbolic SDC propagation analysis to enable incremental re-analysis. When code changes, it analyzes only modified sections rather than entire programs, leveraging compositional analysis to identify vulnerable instructions and guide selective compiler-level SDC detection.
key_novelty: First approach to enable compositional and incremental error injection analysis, reanalyzing only changed program sections rather than running fresh analyses.
contributions: Compositional error injection framework combining empirical and symbolic analyses
3.2× geomean speedup on incremental modifications (up to 17.2×)
Selective instruction protection that minimizes runtime overhead while meeting SDC coverage targets
Practical integration into iterative software development workflows

metrics.speedup: 3.2× geomean on incremental versions; up to 17.2×

limitations: Evaluated on only five benchmark programs; scalability to larger industrial codebases not demonstrated.
